correctness.rationale: An exact cyclic-gap count gives T=n(n-4)(n-5)/6; prescribed-pair counts are 0, n-5, n-6 at separations 1, 2, and >=3, respectively. Fourier summation of the circulant second moments yields the displayed quadratic cosine spectrum; fixed cardinality forces exactly the zero spatial mode. For n>=10 the cosine polynomial is strictly decreasing on sampled points and positive even at c=1; n=7,8,9 are resolved by explicit quadratic vertices and exact isolating rational intervals for the short-degree cosine roots. At n=6 two complementary alternating configurations give rank one. Asymptotic expansion of the exact extremal modes proves the 1+8/n+O(n^-2) sharp squared ratio. Independently enumerated admissible triples and rational covariance rows for n=7..26, checked rational cubic brackets for 7 and 9, and spot-tested modes for 7..1000. These finite tests are not the all-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: The conditional three-particle uniform law has one exact zero spatial mode and positive nonconstant eigenvalues, with unique sharp extremizers and a condition ratio approaching one at the exact rate 8/n. The two closest published cycle-independent-set covariance results concern the full mixture over ALL independent-set sizes and have strictly positive constant modes and a limiting squared ratio five. The complete open-access Vavro manuscript supplies canonical cluster partition counts but not pair-resolved spatial Fourier spectra; Jain et al. treat fixed-size sampling via particle-number Fourier inversion and not these spatial mode bounds. The claimed novelty is restricted to the complete fixed-three sharp spectral classification; simple cluster counting and circulant diagonalization are credited background. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Fixed-particle exclusion models are natural microcanonical objects; their first-harmonic sampling stability is distinct from full Lucas-cube mixtures. At exactly three particles, the two-site correlations exhibit genuine separation-dependent exclusion (three off-diagonal cases), and one obtains a complete all-length sharp rank/condition classification, including the six-to-seven-site identifiability transition, exact longest/shortest wavelength extremizers, and a precise 8/n approach to tightness. This determines a useful natural Fourier reconstruction invariant for an infinite family, not an arbitrary finite table.
